blogs.title: Beyond the Right to Control: The Fifth Circuit’s Boundary Between Information and Property
blogs.description: This post analyzes the doctrinal distinction the Fifth Circuit drew between the 'right-to-control' theory rejected in Ciminelli and the 'fraudulent-inducement' theory. It explores how the court navigated the fine line between depriving a victim of valuable economic information (which is not a property interest) and tricking a victim into parting with money to buy a security (which is), and what this means for the future of federal fraud prosecutions.

blogs.title: Profit Without Pecuniary Loss: Does 'Intent to Defraud' Require an Intent to Harm?
blogs.description: Focusing on the application of the recent Supreme Court decision in Kousisis, this post examines the court's reasoning that a defendant's intent to profit from a scheme satisfies the 'intent to defraud' element, even if the defendant did not specifically intend to cause the victim a net economic loss. It discusses the implications for securities fraud cases where the victim may receive an asset of roughly equivalent market value in exchange for their money.

blogs.title: Finfluencers in the Crosshairs: Traditional Fraud Doctrines in the Social Media Age
blogs.description: This post looks at the case through the lens of modern financial influence, discussing how the 'pump and dump' schemes of the social media era are being fit into traditional statutory frameworks. It considers the legal vulnerabilities of social media traders who misrepresent their positions to followers and whether the court's ruling creates a broader pathway for prosecuting 'finfluencer' activity under 18 U.S.C. § 1348.
